text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Glafcos Clerides issues a stern message to demonstrators not to create incidents today at UDI protests.
- Auditor general starts inquiries into allegations of mismanagement of public funds in tennis court tenders.
- Security tops the agenda as US officials hold talks.
- Staff shortages bring welfare department to breaking point.
- Accusations fly between the government and commercial banks over the latter's refusal to issue loans for property in the occupied areas.
- Disy and Diko parties go their separate ways in municipal elections, supporting different candidates in Nicosia.
- The U.S. seeks examples of intent from the Greek Cypriot side on issues relating to a moratorium in Greek and Turkish fly overs on the island before proceeding with its initiative.
- Guns discovered in Limassol have a criminal past.
- Security along the ceasefire line is stepped up ahead of today's protests.
- Diko disagrees with Disy on supporting the candidacy of Nicosia mayor Lellos Demetriades in next month's municipal elections.
- The government will exclude companies which owe taxes from public tenders.
